blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, invoice and documentation standards become a small but essential discipline. Every invoice must contain the correct legal information: supplier name, tax number, invoice number, date, description, amounts, VAT rate and total. Missing any of these can invalidate the invoice — which means the expense cannot be deducted, even if it was a real expense.

Good teams use a short intake checklist for every supplier invoice that arrives. If anything is missing, the supplier is asked to reissue before the invoice enters the system. That tiny friction early prevents a much bigger problem later, when the auditor looks at a two-year-old missing detail and quietly disallows the cost.

Documentation standards feel pedantic until the first audit. After that, they feel like a quiet investment that everyone wishes they had made earlier.

items.q: According to the text, what can happen if an invoice is missing required fields?
options: The invoice is paid at a lower amount
The invoice can be invalidated and the expense cannot be deducted
items.why: "Missing any of these can invalidate the invoice — which means the expense cannot be deducted."

items.q: When a supplier invoice is missing information, what do good teams do?
options: Forward it straight to the auditor
Pay it and correct the records later
Ask the supplier to reissue before it enters the system
items.why: "the supplier is asked to reissue before the invoice enters the system."

items.q: What does the phrase "That tiny friction early prevents a much bigger problem later" suggest?
options: A small check at intake avoids a costly problem in the audit
items.why: Inferência: o pequeno esforço na entrada evita o custo rejeitado dois anos depois.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Checking invoices at intake is worth the effort
A missing field can cost you the deduction later
Reissuing early is cheaper than fixing it in an audit
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata os padrões como um investimento sensato, não como burocracia inútil.

items.q: The final sentence suggests that people usually value documentation standards…
items.why: Inferência: "they feel like a quiet investment that everyone wishes they had made earlier" — o reconhecimento vem depois da auditoria.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o novo checklist à equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for joining. I want to walk you through the one-page supplier invoice checklist we're rolling out from Monday. It's short on purpose — nine fields, nothing more.

Here's the problem we're solving. Last month I pulled a sample of invoices from the last two years, and quite a few were missing a tax number or a proper description. Nobody noticed at the time, because we were busy and the payments went through. But when the auditor reviews those files, a missing field can mean the cost is disallowed. We could genuinely lose the deduction on real expenses.

So from now on, every invoice gets checked at intake against this list. If a field is missing, we don't process it — we email the supplier and ask them to reissue. I know that adds a little friction, and some suppliers won't love it. But that small delay today is far cheaper than a disallowed cost we discover in a review.

Please don't treat this as optional or something we bend when we're in a hurry. The whole point is that it's automatic. Any questions, come to me directly.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Emily rolling out from Monday?
items.why: "the one-page supplier invoice checklist we're rolling out from Monday."

items.q: What did Emily find when she sampled invoices from the last two years?
options: All of them were fully compliant
The VAT rate was always wrong
Several were missing a tax number or a proper description
items.why: "quite a few were missing a tax number or a proper description."

items.q: What will happen if a field is missing at intake?
options: The invoice is paid and corrected later
The finance team fills in the gap
The invoice is sent straight to the auditor
The invoice is not processed and the supplier is asked to reissue
items.why: "we don't process it — we email the supplier and ask them to reissue."

items.q: Why does Emily accept the small delay the checklist creates?
options: Because it is cheaper than a disallowed cost found in a review
Because it reduces the number of invoices
Because the auditor requires a delay
items.why: Inferência: "that small delay today is far cheaper than a disallowed cost we discover in a review."

items.q: What does Emily mean when she says the check should be "automatic"?
options: It should only apply to large suppliers
It should happen once a year
It should always be applied, never skipped when busy
It should be run by software with no people involved
items.why: Inferência: ela pede que não tratem como opcional nem "dobrem" a regra na pressa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The supplier sent the wrong invoice, so we couldn't pay it." An invoice is…
options: a receipt for a completed payment
a document requesting payment for goods or services
items.why: Invoice = fatura: o documento que pede o pagamento por bens ou serviços.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A missing tax number can ___ the whole invoice, so the cost can't be deducted."
items.why: To invalidate = invalidar: tornar o documento sem validade.

items.q: "The auditor decided to disallow the cost." To disallow a cost means to…
options: refuse to accept it as deductible
items.why: To disallow = rejeitar: não aceitar o custo como dedutível.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We caught the error early thanks to the ___ we run on every invoice that arrives."
items.why: Intake checklist = checklist de entrada, aplicado a cada fatura que chega.

items.q: "Asking suppliers to reissue adds a little friction." Here, friction means…
options: a small amount of resistance or effort
a delay in payment terms only
items.why: Friction = atrito: um pequeno esforço ou resistência no processo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de processos e auditoria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the new checklist." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the checklist to every team next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A couple of suppliers pushed back on the reissue request." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed the standard but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "If we don't catch missing fields at intake, they'll come back to bite us in the audit." This means they will…
options: be fixed by the supplier automatically
cause a serious problem for us later
items.why: Come back to bite us = voltar para nos prejudicar mais tarde.
